details: The European Central Bank (ECB) is widely anticipated to keep interest rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting. Analysts from Bank of America suggest the ECB's communication will mirror its March messaging, with potential rate cuts projected for the near future. However, other strategists believe the ECB may adopt a hawkish tone, signaling rate hikes in June and September due to pipeline inflation and the implications of the Middle East conflict, despite German inflation accelerating less than expected.
title: ECB Expected to Hold Rates, Future Hikes Possible Amid Inflation Concerns

details: Cryptocurrency markets are bracing for a macro-heavy week, including the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, where rates are expected to remain unchanged. Critical US economic data, including Q1 GDP growth and March PCE inflation figures, are scheduled for Thursday, April 30. Analysts warn that persistent inflation could lead to a hawkish Fed tone, potentially causing Bitcoin to pull back.
title: US Fed Meeting and Key Economic Data This Week to Drive Volatility

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has signed new agreements with Nexo Standards, the Berlin Group, and the European Cards Payment Cooperation (ECPC). These deals aim to base digital euro online payments on existing open technical standards, marking a significant technical milestone as the project targets a potential 2029 issuance.
title: ECB Forges Ahead with Digital Euro Payment Standards

details: The total cryptocurrency market capitalization climbed by approximately 10% in April 2026 to around $2.7 trillion, with Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) rising 16% and 14% respectively. April also marked the strongest monthly net inflows into spot Bitcoin ETFs since October 2025, driven by significant institutional demand. Despite this positive performance, some prominent crypto investors, like Michael Novogratz, remain cautious about Bitcoin crossing $100,000 this year, citing resistance levels.
title: Crypto Market Sees Recovery and Strong Bitcoin ETF Inflows in April

details: The International Monetary Fund's (IMF) April 2026 World Economic Outlook emphasizes the significant impact of geopolitical risks, particularly the war in the Middle East and the resulting energy shock, on global economies, especially in Asia. The report stresses the need for countries to prioritize policies that enhance resilience and adaptability to these evolving risks.
title: IMF Highlights Geopolitical and Energy Shock Risks in Global Economy
